newsitem.title: CANADA: WestJet says to return to skies on Oct 4.
newsitem.headline: WestJet says to return to skies on Oct 4.

text.p: WestJet Airlines Ltd said on Monday it planned to resume flight operations on October 4 with an abbreviated schedule following a green light from Transport Canada.

"As you can imagine we are extremely angered by the events that have taken place to date and we continue to feel that we have been unjustly treated," Clive Beddoe, chairman and chief executive of WestJet, said in a statement.
"We must however accept the fact that Transport Canada is the regulatory body who has absolute authority over our industry."
Transport Canada, the country's main transportation regulator, said on Monday it lifted WestJet Airlines Ltd's notice of impending suspension.
WestJet voluntarily grounded its fleet on September 17 after Transport Canada said the airline was not following approved maintenance procedures.
The no-frills carrier said it would be aloft on Friday using three of its four planes. The fourth would be phased in shortly after.

The company also said it would offer a reduced one-way fare of C$45 between Alberta and cities in other western Canadian provinces through October. The fare cut was being made to thank its customers for their support while WestJet's planes were grounded, it said.
